steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: A training year (macrocycle) is divided into distinct phases, each with specific training goals. The training programme is structured so the athlete peaks (reaches their best performance) at the right time - usually for the most important competitions. | Goal: Build a base of fitness and develop the specific skills needed for the upcoming competitive season. The aim is to prepare the body and mind for the demands of competition. | Goal: Maintain the fitness built in pre-season while performing at the highest possible level in competitions. Training shifts from building fitness to maintaining it and peaking for key events. | Tapering: A planned reduction in training volume (by 40-60%) in the 7-14 days before a major competition.
